# Solo Frontend — Complete AI Task Prompts

```text
MASTER EXECUTION PROTOCOL — READ ONCE BEFORE EXECUTING ANY PHASE

This Markdown file is the canonical execution plan for the Solo frontend.

Before changing any code:
1. Read this entire Markdown file from top to bottom once.
2. Build a complete mental model of all phases, task dependencies, shared architecture, frozen product rules, constraints, and later integration requirements.
3. Keep the full file as active working context for the duration of the current execution session. Do not repeatedly ask the user to resend or restate requirements already present here.
4. Inspect the current repository, Git history, current branch, existing commits, and implementation state before deciding where execution should begin.

PHASE EXECUTION MODE
When the user says, for example, "Execute Phase 1", execute the entire requested phase end-to-end.
- Execute every task in that phase in dependency order.
- Do not wait for user confirmation between tasks.
- Do not stop after producing a plan; actually implement the tasks.
- Use all other tasks and phases as architectural context so work done now remains compatible with later phases.
- It is acceptable and expected to create shared foundations required by the current task even when later tasks consume them. Do not artificially avoid correct architecture merely because another task appears later in the file.
- At the start of the phase, determine which tasks are already fully complete from repository state and Git history. Validate them against their acceptance criteria and resume from the first incomplete task rather than blindly duplicating completed work.
- Never mark a task complete merely because similarly named code exists. Verify its implementation and acceptance criteria.

TASK COMPLETION LOOP
For each task in the requested phase, follow this loop without asking for permission to continue:
1. Re-read the current task prompt and all dependency task outcomes relevant to it.
2. Inspect the current code before editing.
3. Implement the task completely, including required UI states, contracts, mocks, permissions/capabilities, i18n, RTL/LTR, responsive behavior, accessibility, security constraints, and tests described by that task.
4. Run formatting and static checks available at this stage.
5. Run the complete test and validation suite that exists and is meaningful at this stage of the repository, including at minimum all currently configured lint, typecheck, unit/integration tests, build, and task-relevant end-to-end/accessibility/visual checks when those systems exist.
6. Fix every failure caused by the task. Do not commit a knowingly broken state.
7. Re-run the required checks until they pass.
8. Review git diff and git status for accidental changes, secrets, generated junk, unrelated rewrites, or missing files.
9. Commit the completed task on the current working branch only after validation passes. Use a clear commit message containing the task ID and title, for example: `feat(F1-003): implement phone recovery flows`.
10. Record the commit SHA in the running execution report.
11. Immediately continue to the next task in dependency order.

COMMIT AND GIT RULES
- One completed task should normally produce one focused commit.
- Do not combine several completed task IDs into one commit unless an unavoidable atomic migration genuinely spans those tasks; if that happens, state the reason in the final report.
- Do not commit failing tests, unresolved TypeScript errors, lint failures, broken builds, conflict markers, secrets, local environment files, temporary debug code, or unrelated generated artifacts.
- Do not amend, squash, rebase, reset, force-push, or rewrite existing history unless the user explicitly requests it.
- Do not push commits to a remote unless the user explicitly asks for a push.
- Preserve user-authored changes that are unrelated to the current task.

FAILURE / BLOCKER RULE
- If a true blocker prevents correct completion of the current task, do not skip it and continue as though the phase were complete.
- Investigate and make the best safe effort to resolve it using the repository and this file.
- If it remains genuinely blocked, stop the phase at that task, leave the repository in the safest non-broken state possible, do not create a false "completed" commit, and report the blocker, evidence, attempted fixes, and exact next action.
- A product-discovery question is not a blocker when the frozen requirements in this file already imply a safe implementation choice.

PHASE COMPLETION
A phase is complete only when every task in that phase has passed its acceptance criteria, required validation is green, and each completed task has an associated commit.
At the end of the requested phase, provide one concise execution report containing:
- completed task IDs in order,
- commit SHA for each task,
- checks/tests executed and their final status,
- migrations or architectural decisions made,
- any intentionally deferred items explicitly allowed by the task prompts,
- remaining blockers, if any,
- final git status.

Do not ask for confirmation between tasks. Continue automatically until the requested phase is complete or a genuine blocker makes safe progress impossible.
```

# Phase 0 — Foundation

## F0-001 — Repository Restructure to /frontend + /backend

```text
You are the AI Coding Agent implementing F0-001 — Repository Restructure to /frontend + /backend for Solo.
REPOSITORY AND EXECUTION CONTEXT
- Canonical repository: Solo-Students-Managment/Solo
- Primary implementation path: /frontend
- Phase: Phase 0 — Foundation
- Phase goal: Build the repository, architecture, design system, mock/network layer, identity/context foundations, shared primitives, testing, security, PWA/realtime and quality gates required by every later feature.
- Dependencies that must already be complete or intentionally stubbed by prior approved tasks: None
- The current product scope is frozen. Frontend is greenfield Next.js; legacy Vite code is reference-only unless an independently useful asset/utility was deliberately retained.

READ BEFORE CODING
- Scope is frozen. Do not ask new product-discovery questions and do not invent new features. If a true implementation blocker remains, choose the smallest behavior consistent with the frozen requirements and document it; only surface a blocker when a safe implementation cannot be inferred.
- Before editing, inspect the current repository and relevant feature code. Read docs/frontend/ENGINEERING_RULES.md and docs/frontend/PROJECT_CONTEXT.md when they exist; if this task creates them or they do not exist yet, use the frozen rules in this Markdown file and the current repository state as the source of truth. Do not rewrite previous features or shared infrastructure without a concrete need.
- Work only in /frontend unless this task explicitly updates root documentation or the /backend placeholder. Do not implement a real backend, database, server authorization, payment processor, storage service or WebSocket server.
- Use Next.js App Router + TypeScript strict + pnpm, feature-first boundaries, shared Solo design-system primitives and typed contracts.
- Use TanStack Query for server state, Zustand only for true global UI state, local React state for local UI, URL search params for shareable filters/sort/page/tab state, React Hook Form + Zod for forms and MSW for development network simulation.
- All meaningful UI text must be localized through fa/en i18n. Support true RTL/LTR, Light/Dark, Desktop/Tablet/Mobile, keyboard access and WCAG 2.2 AA.
- Use Effective Capabilities for UI access and disabled reasons. Never scatter role/plan permission logic through random components. Backend remains the future authorization source of truth.
- Preserve strict persona/context/organization isolation in query keys, caches, routes, realtime subscriptions, offline state and UI persistence.
- Never persist password, OTP, access token, refresh token, private API secret or equivalent credentials in localStorage. Never leak PII/private content into URL, telemetry or logs.
- Use existing shared primitives (SoloDataTable, SoloForm, SoloFeedback, SoloCalendar, SoloCharts, SoloUploader, SoloContentEditor, SoloPrint, SoloMap, realtime/PWA clients) instead of inventing duplicate local systems when their dependencies are already available.
- Implement Loading, Empty, Error, Not Found, Forbidden, Disabled-with-reason, Offline/Retry and plan/usage-limited states only where relevant to this task; do not add irrelevant states mechanically.
- Do not hide real blockers with fake business logic. Mocks may simulate future contracts, but the frontend must remain replaceable by real backend implementations later.

FROZEN PRODUCT RULES RELEVANT TO THIS TASK
- Do not implement product business features unless the task explicitly asks for a shared primitive or infrastructure slice.
- Keep /frontend isolated from future /backend and avoid real backend logic in client-side mocks.
- Preserve greenfield architecture and do not silently port Vite/React Router/Formik/Yup patterns into Next.js.

TASK-SPECIFIC IMPLEMENTATION CHECKLIST
- Audit the current root Vite application and package-manager artifacts before moving/removing anything.
- Create the approved /frontend and /backend boundaries; /backend receives only a placeholder README.
- Preserve useful docs and Git history; update root README to make the organization repository canonical.
- Do not port legacy UI/routes/localStorage business mocks into the new frontend.

ARCHITECTURE AND INTEGRATION REQUIREMENTS
- Place code in the approved feature-first boundaries. app/ should remain routing/layout/page composition; keep feature internals inside their feature and expose only deliberate public APIs.
- Define or extend typed request/response/domain contracts and Zod boundaries only where this task needs them. Use standard Solo API error, money, date/time, opaque ID, concurrency and file conventions as applicable.
- Add MSW handlers/fixtures for the exact APIs used by this slice, including realistic success and meaningful failure states. Do not add unrelated mock endpoints.
- Use context-scoped TanStack Query keys and invalidation/mutation behavior. If the task is purely visual/infrastructure and consumes no server data, do not introduce artificial Query/MSW code.
- Route construction must use typed route helpers and the approved deep-link/search-param convention. Never put PII or sensitive identifiers in URLs.
- If the task touches realtime, offline, uploads, editor, maps, charts, forms, tables, print or feedback, integrate the existing shared foundation instead of implementing a parallel local version.

UI / UX REQUIREMENTS
- Use the Solo design language: modern, professional, educational, clean and readable; friendly without being childish; data-dense only where management workflows need it; no card-everywhere or decorative glassmorphism.
- Provide responsive behavior for desktop, tablet and mobile/PWA. No critical feature may be desktop-only.
- Support fa/en, true RTL/LTR, Light/Dark and reduced-motion preferences. Do not hardcode important UI copy.
- Use clear hierarchy, accessible labels/help/error copy, proper focus management, keyboard navigation and semantic HTML.
- Expose disabled/blocked reasons when useful (upgrade required, permission missing, usage limit, policy restriction, account restriction, reauth required) rather than silently hiding important affordances.
- For complex management screens, use the shared DataTable/Form/Drawer/Modal/Saved View patterns; for mobile, redesign information density rather than squeezing desktop tables unchanged.

SECURITY, PRIVACY AND TENANCY
- Treat frontend permission gates as UX only; never imply they are server authorization.
- Verify organization/personal/subject context isolation for all data, cache keys, URLs, realtime/offline state and mutations touched by this task.
- Sanitize rich HTML, validate external URLs and protect private downloads where relevant.
- Never log/persist password, OTP, auth token, private message content, protected file contents or other sensitive data.
- Sensitive actions defined by product policy must use online-only behavior, re-authentication, confirmation/impact preview, approval and audit-aware contracts where applicable.

TESTING REQUIREMENTS
- Add focused unit tests for pure business-facing UI logic, formatters/selectors/validation introduced by this task.
- Add React Testing Library interaction tests for important component/form/permission/error behavior.
- Add or extend Playwright smoke/E2E for the critical happy path and at least the most important denial/failure path when this task creates a user workflow.
- Verify affected fa/en, RTL/LTR, Light/Dark, desktop/mobile and accessibility behavior. Use automated a11y checks plus manual keyboard/focus review for critical flows.
- If the task affects plan/capability/context/offline/realtime behavior, include fixtures/tests for those state transitions and leakage boundaries.
- Run the relevant lint, typecheck, tests and build before finishing. Do not report completion with failing required checks.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- All task-specific acceptance criteria are implemented; no unexplained TODO, placeholder or fake completion remains.
- TypeScript strict typecheck, lint and production build pass for the affected frontend.
- Required unit/component tests pass; critical user flows have Playwright smoke/E2E coverage appropriate to the task.
- Relevant Loading/Empty/Error/Forbidden/Disabled/Offline/limit states are implemented and tested.
- Desktop/Tablet/Mobile, fa/en, RTL/LTR, Light/Dark and keyboard/screen-reader behavior are verified for affected UI.
- Effective Capabilities, persona/context isolation and privacy boundaries are validated for all affected actions/data.
- Mock API behavior matches typed future contracts; feature UI does not import seed data directly or implement server business logic.
- No secrets or sensitive private content are introduced into client persistence, URLs, logs or telemetry.
- Shared components are reused; new shared abstractions are documented if genuinely necessary.
- Performance/bundle impact is reasonable and no avoidable regression is introduced.
- The final agent report lists changed files, commands/tests executed, acceptance status, assumptions and real blockers.

OUT OF SCOPE
- Real backend/database/server authorization implementation.
- Real payment processor, SMS provider, map provider secret, file scanner/storage service or WebSocket server integration unless a later backend task explicitly supplies it.
- Marketing landing website implementation.
- Product features belonging to later sibling tasks/phases unless a small shared contract is strictly necessary for this task.
- New product discovery or scope expansion.

FINAL RESPONSE FROM THE CODING AGENT
1. Summarize what was implemented and any deliberate design/architecture decisions.
2. List every changed/added/deleted file.
3. List commands/tests run and their result.
4. Report acceptance-criteria status and any remaining real blocker/assumption.
5. Do not claim completion if required checks or critical states are missing.
```

- Use the Solo design language: modern, professional, educational, clean and readable; friendly without being childish; data-dense only where management workflows need it; no card-everywhere or decorative glassmorphism.
- Provide responsive behavior for desktop, tablet and mobile/PWA. No critical feature may be desktop-only.
- Support fa/en, true RTL/LTR, Light/Dark and reduced-motion preferences. Do not hardcode important UI copy.
- Use clear hierarchy, accessible labels/help/error copy, proper focus management, keyboard navigation and semantic HTML.
- Expose disabled/blocked reasons when useful (upgrade required, permission missing, usage limit, policy restriction, account restriction, reauth required) rather than silently hiding important affordances.
- For complex management screens, use the shared DataTable/Form/Drawer/Modal/Saved View patterns; for mobile, redesign information density rather than squeezing desktop tables unchanged.

- Treat frontend permission gates as UX only; never imply they are server authorization.
- Verify organization/personal/subject context isolation for all data, cache keys, URLs, realtime/offline state and mutations touched by this task.

- Never log/persist password, OTP, auth token, private message content, protected file contents or other sensitive data.
- Sensitive actions defined by product policy must use online-only behavior, re-authentication, confirmation/impact preview, approval and audit-aware contracts where applicable.

TESTING REQUIREMENTS
- Add focused unit tests for pure business-facing UI logic, formatters/selectors/validation introduced by this task.
- Add React Testing Library interaction tests for important component/form/permission/error behavior.
- Add or extend Playwright smoke/E2E for the critical happy path and at least the most important denial/failure path when this task creates a user workflow.
- Verify affected fa/en, RTL/LTR, Light/Dark, desktop/mobile and accessibility behavior. Use automated a11y checks plus manual keyboard/focus review for critical flows.
- If the task affects plan/capability/context/offline/realtime behavior, include fixtures/tests for those state transitions and leakage boundaries.
- Run the relevant lint, typecheck, tests and build before finishing. Do not report completion with failing required checks.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- All task-specific acceptance criteria are implemented; no unexplained TODO, placeholder or fake completion remains.
- TypeScript strict typecheck, lint and production build pass for the affected frontend.
- Required unit/component tests pass; critical user flows have Playwright smoke/E2E coverage appropriate to the task.
- Relevant Loading/Empty/Error/Forbidden/Disabled/Offline/limit states are implemented and tested.
- Desktop/Tablet/Mobile, fa/en, RTL/LTR, Light/Dark and keyboard/screen-reader behavior are verified for affected UI.
- Effective Capabilities, persona/context isolation and privacy boundaries are validated for all affected actions/data.
- Mock API behavior matches typed future contracts; feature UI does not import seed data directly or implement server business logic.
- No secrets or sensitive private content are introduced into client persistence, URLs, logs or telemetry.
- Shared components are reused; new shared abstractions are documented if genuinely necessary.
- Performance/bundle impact is reasonable and no avoidable regression is introduced.
- The final agent report lists changed files, commands/tests executed, acceptance status, assumptions and real blockers.

OUT OF SCOPE
- Real backend/database/server authorization implementation.
- Real payment processor, SMS provider, map provider secret, file scanner/storage service or WebSocket server integration unless a later backend task explicitly supplies it.
- Marketing landing website implementation.
- Product features belonging to later sibling tasks/phases unless a small shared contract is strictly necessary for this task.

- Use Next.js App Router + TypeScript strict + pnpm, feature-first boundaries, shared Solo design-system primitives and typed contracts.
- Use TanStack Query for server state, Zustand only for true global UI state, local React state for local UI, URL search params for shareable filters/sort/page/tab state, React Hook Form + Zod for forms and MSW for development network simulation.
- All meaningful UI text must be localized through fa/en i18n. Support true RTL/LTR, Light/Dark, Desktop/Tablet/Mobile, keyboard access and WCAG 2.2 AA.
- Use Effective Capabilities for UI access and disabled reasons. Never scatter role/plan permission logic through random components. Backend remains the future authorization source of truth.
- Preserve strict persona/context/organization isolation in query keys, caches, routes, realtime subscriptions, offline state and UI persistence.
- Never persist password, OTP, access token, refresh token, private API secret or equivalent credentials in localStorage. Never leak PII/private content into URL, telemetry or logs.
- Use existing shared primitives (SoloDataTable, SoloForm, SoloFeedback, SoloCalendar, SoloCharts, SoloUploader, SoloContentEditor, SoloPrint, SoloMap, realtime/PWA clients) instead of inventing duplicate local systems when their dependencies are already available.
- Implement Loading, Empty, Error, Not Found, Forbidden, Disabled-with-reason, Offline/Retry and plan/usage-limited states only where relevant to this task; do not add irrelevant states mechanically.
- Do not hide real blockers with fake business logic. Mocks may simulate future contracts, but the frontend must remain replaceable by real backend implementations later.

FROZEN PRODUCT RULES RELEVANT TO THIS TASK
- One account may have multiple personas. Teacher persona is self-activated and defaults to Teacher Free; Student and Guardian personas activate only from real relationships.
- Global Home, Persona Switcher, Context Switcher and Subject Switcher are distinct and must remain context-safe.
- Effective Capabilities are the only UI access source and include allowed + reason; do not hardcode scattered role/plan checks.
- Context switch must invalidate/scope query caches, realtime subscriptions and persisted UI state to prevent cross-tenant leakage.
- Phone is the primary identity; signup uses first name, last name, calling-code + phone, OTP verification and password.
- Normal login supports phone + password and optional OTP login; email is optional, unverified and not a login identifier.
- 2FA supports SMS OTP/TOTP/recovery codes; normal users optional, organization may require sensitive roles, Admin Solo mandatory.
- Production session design is HttpOnly Secure Cookie; never expose token management to UI/localStorage.
- Sensitive actions use re-auth. Device/session management and session expiry/revoke are first-class.

- Implement the complete frontend slice for “Teacher Persona Activation & Teacher Global Dashboard” without pulling sibling-phase scope forward unless it is required by an existing shared contract.

Read docs/frontend/ENGINEERING_RULES.md and docs/frontend/PROJECT_CONTEXT.md when they exist; if this task creates them or they do not exist yet, use the frozen rules in this Markdown file and the current repository state as the source of truth. Do not rewrite previous features or shared infrastructure without a concrete need.
- Work only in /frontend unless this task explicitly updates root documentation or the /backend placeholder. Do not implement a real backend, database, server authorization, payment processor, storage service or WebSocket server.
- Use Next.js App Router + TypeScript strict + pnpm, feature-first boundaries, shared Solo design-system primitives and typed contracts.
- Use TanStack Query for server state, Zustand only for true global UI state, local React state for local UI, URL search params for shareable filters/sort/page/tab state, React Hook Form + Zod for forms and MSW for development network simulation.
- All meaningful UI text must be localized through fa/en i18n. Support true RTL/LTR, Light/Dark, Desktop/Tablet/Mobile, keyboard access and WCAG 2.2 AA.
- Use Effective Capabilities for UI access and disabled reasons. Never scatter role/plan permission logic through random components. Backend remains the future authorization source of truth.
- Preserve strict persona/context/organization isolation in query keys, caches, routes, realtime subscriptions, offline state and UI persistence.
- Never persist password, OTP, access token, refresh token, private API secret or equivalent credentials in localStorage. Never leak PII/private content into URL, telemetry or logs.
- Use existing shared primitives (SoloDataTable, SoloForm, SoloFeedback, SoloCalendar, SoloCharts, SoloUploader, SoloContentEditor, SoloPrint, SoloMap, realtime/PWA clients) instead of inventing duplicate local systems when their dependencies are already available.
- Implement Loading, Empty, Error, Not Found, Forbidden, Disabled-with-reason, Offline/Retry and plan/usage-limited states only where relevant to this task; do not add irrelevant states mechanically.
- Do not hide real blockers with fake business logic. Mocks may simulate future contracts, but the frontend must remain replaceable by real backend implementations later.

FROZEN PRODUCT RULES RELEVANT TO THIS TASK
- Assignment types include Homework/Project/Essay/Presentation/Research/Practice/Custom; support deadlines, rubric, resources, submission, feedback, status and versions.
- Targets can be subject/classes/students, with shared + individualized assignments and future-student inclusion policy.
- Allowed submission types include PDF/Word/Image/Audio; no direct video upload.
- Advanced flow supports group teams, peer review, revisions, grade release states and grade-change notifications/history.
- Student may have multiple subjects and different teachers; teacher may teach multiple subjects. Subject has its own level/evaluation/grade/progress/notification settings.
- Enrollment/StudentSubject is the relationship model; do not move subject-specific fields onto the Student base entity.
- Add student by name + unique phone; link existing identity or create invite/SMS/signup flow.
- Enrollment statuses are Active, Completed, Withdrawn, Failed, Transferred; completed history remains read-only/history and does not count active.
- Teacher/class transfer preserves educational history and respects private-message boundaries.
- Use SoloUploader contracts and file security states Queued/Uploading/Scanning/Safe/Blocked/Failed (and Scan Failed where contract distinguishes). File is unavailable until Safe.
- Enforce plan/context/feature file policies, protected temporary downloads, versioning, replace/restore/history and quota display.
- Never expose permanent private file URLs or store sensitive file data in insecure browser persistence.

TASK-SPECIFIC IMPLEMENTATION CHECKLIST
- Implement the complete frontend slice for “Assignments & Submission Core” without pulling sibling-phase scope forward unless it is required by an existing shared contract.
- Provide create/edit flows with typed validation, dirty-state handling, explicit success/error feedback, permission-aware fields and safe optimistic behavior only where appropriate.
- Implement realistic MSW fixtures/scenarios only for the APIs this task actually consumes; do not create irrelevant endpoints just to satisfy boilerplate.

ARCHITECTURE AND INTEGRATION REQUIREMENTS
- Place code in the approved feature-first boundaries. app/ should remain routing/layout/page composition; keep feature internals inside their feature and expose only deliberate public APIs.
- Define or extend typed request/response/domain contracts and Zod boundaries only where this task needs them. Use standard Solo API error, money, date/time, opaque ID, concurrency and file conventions as applicable.
- Add MSW handlers/fixtures for the exact APIs used by this slice, including realistic success and meaningful failure states. Do not add unrelated mock endpoints.
- Use context-scoped TanStack Query keys and invalidation/mutation behavior. If the task is purely visual/infrastructure and consumes no server data, do not introduce artificial Query/MSW code.
- Route construction must use typed route helpers and the approved deep-link/search-param convention. Never put PII or sensitive identifiers in URLs.
- If the task touches realtime, offline, uploads, editor, maps, charts, forms, tables, print or feedback, integrate the existing shared foundation instead of implementing a parallel local version.

UI / UX REQUIREMENTS
- Use the Solo design language: modern, professional, educational, clean and readable; friendly without being childish; data-dense only where management workflows need it; no card-everywhere or decorative glassmorphism.
- Provide responsive behavior for desktop, tablet and mobile/PWA. No critical feature may be desktop-only.
- Support fa/en, true RTL/LTR, Light/Dark and reduced-motion preferences. Do not hardcode important UI copy.
- Use clear hierarchy, accessible labels/help/error copy, proper focus management, keyboard navigation and semantic HTML.
- Expose disabled/blocked reasons when useful (upgrade required, permission missing, usage limit, policy restriction, account restriction, reauth required) rather than silently hiding important affordances.
- For complex management screens, use the shared DataTable/Form/Drawer/Modal/Saved View patterns; for mobile, redesign information density rather than squeezing desktop tables unchanged.

- Treat frontend permission gates as UX only; never imply they are server authorization.
- Verify organization/personal/subject context isolation for all data, cache keys, URLs, realtime/offline state and mutations touched by this task.
- Sanitize rich HTML, validate external URLs and protect private downloads where relevant.
- Never log/persist password, OTP, auth token, private message content, protected file contents or other sensitive data.
- Sensitive actions defined by product policy must use online-only behavior, re-authentication, confirmation/impact preview, approval and audit-aware contracts where applicable.

TESTING REQUIREMENTS
- Add focused unit tests for pure business-facing UI logic, formatters/selectors/validation introduced by this task.
- Add React Testing Library interaction tests for important component/form/permission/error behavior.
- Add or extend Playwright smoke/E2E for the critical happy path and at least the most important denial/failure path when this task creates a user workflow.
- Verify affected fa/en, RTL/LTR, Light/Dark, desktop/mobile and accessibility behavior. Use automated a11y checks plus manual keyboard/focus review for critical flows.
- If the task affects plan/capability/context/offline/realtime behavior, include fixtures/tests for those state transitions and leakage boundaries.

OUT OF SCOPE

- Real payment processor, SMS provider, map provider secret, file scanner/storage service or WebSocket server integration unless a later backend task explicitly supplies it.

- Product features belonging to later sibling tasks/phases unless a small shared contract is strictly necessary for this task.

- Preserve strict persona/context/organization isolation in query keys, caches, routes, realtime subscriptions, offline state and UI persistence.
- Never persist password, OTP, access token, refresh token, private API secret or equivalent credentials in localStorage. Never leak PII/private content into URL, telemetry or logs.
- Use existing shared primitives (SoloDataTable, SoloForm, SoloFeedback, SoloCalendar, SoloCharts, SoloUploader, SoloContentEditor, SoloPrint, SoloMap, realtime/PWA clients) instead of inventing duplicate local systems when their dependencies are already available.
- Implement Loading, Empty, Error, Not Found, Forbidden, Disabled-with-reason, Offline/Retry and plan/usage-limited states only where relevant to this task; do not add irrelevant states mechanically.
- Do not hide real blockers with fake business logic. Mocks may simulate future contracts, but the frontend must remain replaceable by real backend implementations later.

FROZEN PRODUCT RULES RELEVANT TO THIS TASK
- Report Card/Transcript/Certificate/Credential outputs require publish/version/branding/permission states and backend-ready official PDF contracts.
- Transcript includes broad educational history but excludes private messages/notes/audit content.
- Public verification exposes minimal information via ID/QR and supports Valid/Replaced/Revoked/expiry as appropriate.
- Recommendation letters support template/editor/workflow/AI draft with human approval.
- Respect Privacy Center, account deletion/deactivation/retention/anonymization, minor safety, block/restrict/report and support recovery policies.

- Sensitive actions are online-only and use re-auth plus approval/impact preview where defined.

- Implement the complete frontend slice for “Certificates Transcript Credentials Public Verification” without pulling sibling-phase scope forward unless it is required by an existing shared contract.

- Use the Solo design language: modern, professional, educational, clean and readable; friendly without being childish; data-dense only where management workflows need it; no card-everywhere or decorative glassmorphism.
- Provide responsive behavior for desktop, tablet and mobile/PWA. No critical feature may be desktop-only.
- Support fa/en, true RTL/LTR, Light/Dark and reduced-motion preferences. Do not hardcode important UI copy.
- Use clear hierarchy, accessible labels/help/error copy, proper focus management, keyboard navigation and semantic HTML.

- Add focused unit tests for pure business-facing UI logic, formatters/selectors/validation introduced by this task.
- Add React Testing Library interaction tests for important component/form/permission/error behavior.
- Add or extend Playwright smoke/E2E for the critical happy path and at least the most important denial/failure path when this task creates a user workflow.
- Verify affected fa/en, RTL/LTR, Light/Dark, desktop/mobile and accessibility behavior. Use automated a11y checks plus manual keyboard/focus review for critical flows.
- If the task affects plan/capability/context/offline/realtime behavior, include fixtures/tests for those state transitions and leakage boundaries.

- Real payment processor, SMS provider, map provider secret, file scanner/storage service or WebSocket server integration unless a later backend task explicitly supplies it.

Do not rewrite previous features or shared infrastructure without a concrete need.
- Work only in /frontend unless this task explicitly updates root documentation or the /backend placeholder. Do not implement a real backend, database, server authorization, payment processor, storage service or WebSocket server.

- Use TanStack Query for server state, Zustand only for true global UI state, local React state for local UI, URL search params for shareable filters/sort/page/tab state, React Hook Form + Zod for forms and MSW for development network simulation.
- All meaningful UI text must be localized through fa/en i18n. Support true RTL/LTR, Light/Dark, Desktop/Tablet/Mobile, keyboard access and WCAG 2.2 AA.
- Use Effective Capabilities for UI access and disabled reasons. Never scatter role/plan permission logic through random components. Backend remains the future authorization source of truth.
- Preserve strict persona/context/organization isolation in query keys, caches, routes, realtime subscriptions, offline state and UI persistence.
- Never persist password, OTP, access token, refresh token, private API secret or equivalent credentials in localStorage. Never leak PII/private content into URL, telemetry or logs.
- Use existing shared primitives (SoloDataTable, SoloForm, SoloFeedback, SoloCalendar, SoloCharts, SoloUploader, SoloContentEditor, SoloPrint, SoloMap, realtime/PWA clients) instead of inventing duplicate local systems when their dependencies are already available.
- Implement Loading, Empty, Error, Not Found, Forbidden, Disabled-with-reason, Offline/Retry and plan/usage-limited states only where relevant to this task; do not add irrelevant states mechanically.
- Do not hide real blockers with fake business logic. Mocks may simulate future contracts, but the frontend must remain replaceable by real backend implementations later.

FROZEN PRODUCT RULES RELEVANT TO THIS TASK
- Use granular roles/permissions with Owner/Manager/Academic Manager/Teacher/Finance/Support-Staff defaults plus custom roles and branch scope.
- Organization Policy Center supports inheritance/override, effective dates, sensitive policy review/publish, impact preview, versions/rollback/audit.
- Approval Center centralizes multi-step sequential/parallel approval, delegation, request-changes, low-risk bulk, SLA/escalation and self-approval prevention.
- Immutable audit is non-editable/non-deletable and captures actor/action/target/context/before-after/reason/security metadata.
- Respect Privacy Center, account deletion/deactivation/retention/anonymization, minor safety, block/restrict/report and support recovery policies.
- Do not leak PII through URL, logs, error telemetry, browser storage, unauthorized search results or cross-context caches.
- Sensitive actions are online-only and use re-auth plus approval/impact preview where defined.

TASK-SPECIFIC IMPLEMENTATION CHECKLIST
- Implement the complete frontend slice for “Organization Policy Center” without pulling sibling-phase scope forward unless it is required by an existing shared contract.
- Provide the primary list/dashboard/detail/configuration surfaces needed by this task, using the shared App Shell, DataTable/Form/Feedback primitives where applicable.
- Provide create/edit flows with typed validation, dirty-state handling, explicit success/error feedback, permission-aware fields and safe optimistic behavior only where appropriate.
- Implement realistic MSW fixtures/scenarios only for the APIs this task actually consumes; do not create irrelevant endpoints just to satisfy boilerplate.

ARCHITECTURE AND INTEGRATION REQUIREMENTS
- Place code in the approved feature-first boundaries. app/ should remain routing/layout/page composition; keep feature internals inside their feature and expose only deliberate public APIs.
- Define or extend typed request/response/domain contracts and Zod boundaries only where this task needs them. Use standard Solo API error, money, date/time, opaque ID, concurrency and file conventions as applicable.
- Add MSW handlers/fixtures for the exact APIs used by this slice, including realistic success and meaningful failure states. Do not add unrelated mock endpoints.
- Use context-scoped TanStack Query keys and invalidation/mutation behavior. If the task is purely visual/infrastructure and consumes no server data, do not introduce artificial Query/MSW code.
- Route construction must use typed route helpers and the approved deep-link/search-param convention. Never put PII or sensitive identifiers in URLs.
- If the task touches realtime, offline, uploads, editor, maps, charts, forms, tables, print or feedback, integrate the existing shared foundation instead of implementing a parallel local version.

UI / UX REQUIREMENTS
- Use the Solo design language: modern, professional, educational, clean and readable; friendly without being childish; data-dense only where management workflows need it; no card-everywhere or decorative glassmorphism.
- Provide responsive behavior for desktop, tablet and mobile/PWA. No critical feature may be desktop-only.
- Support fa/en, true RTL/LTR, Light/Dark and reduced-motion preferences. Do not hardcode important UI copy.
- Use clear hierarchy, accessible labels/help/error copy, proper focus management, keyboard navigation and semantic HTML.
- Expose disabled/blocked reasons when useful (upgrade required, permission missing, usage limit, policy restriction, account restriction, reauth required) rather than silently hiding important affordances.
- For complex management screens, use the shared DataTable/Form/Drawer/Modal/Saved View patterns; for mobile, redesign information density rather than squeezing desktop tables unchanged.

SECURITY, PRIVACY AND TENANCY
- Treat frontend permission gates as UX only; never imply they are server authorization.
- Verify organization/personal/subject context isolation for all data, cache keys, URLs, realtime/offline state and mutations touched by this task.
- Sanitize rich HTML, validate external URLs and protect private downloads where relevant.
- Never log/persist password, OTP, auth token, private message content, protected file contents or other sensitive data.
- Sensitive actions defined by product policy must use online-only behavior, re-authentication, confirmation/impact preview, approval and audit-aware contracts where applicable.

TESTING REQUIREMENTS
- Add focused unit tests for pure business-facing UI logic, formatters/selectors/validation introduced by this task.
- Add React Testing Library interaction tests for important component/form/permission/error behavior.
- Add or extend Playwright smoke/E2E for the critical happy path and at least the most important denial/failure path when this task creates a user workflow.
- Verify affected fa/en, RTL/LTR, Light/Dark, desktop/mobile and accessibility behavior. Use automated a11y checks plus manual keyboard/focus review for critical flows.
- If the task affects plan/capability/context/offline/realtime behavior, include fixtures/tests for those state transitions and leakage boundaries.
- Run the relevant lint, typecheck, tests and build before finishing. Do not report completion with failing required checks.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- All task-specific acceptance criteria are implemented; no unexplained TODO, placeholder or fake completion remains.
- TypeScript strict typecheck, lint and production build pass for the affected frontend.
- Required unit/component tests pass; critical user flows have Playwright smoke/E2E coverage appropriate to the task.
- Relevant Loading/Empty/Error/Forbidden/Disabled/Offline/limit states are implemented and tested.
- Desktop/Tablet/Mobile, fa/en, RTL/LTR, Light/Dark and keyboard/screen-reader behavior are verified for affected UI.
- Effective Capabilities, persona/context isolation and privacy boundaries are validated for all affected actions/data.
- Mock API behavior matches typed future contracts; feature UI does not import seed data directly or implement server business logic.
- No secrets or sensitive private content are introduced into client persistence, URLs, logs or telemetry.
- Shared components are reused; new shared abstractions are documented if genuinely necessary.
- Performance/bundle impact is reasonable and no avoidable regression is introduced.
- The final agent report lists changed files, commands/tests executed, acceptance status, assumptions and real blockers.

OUT OF SCOPE
- Real backend/database/server authorization implementation.
- Real payment processor, SMS provider, map provider secret, file scanner/storage service or WebSocket server integration unless a later backend task explicitly supplies it.
- Marketing landing website implementation.
- Product features belonging to later sibling tasks/phases unless a small shared contract is strictly necessary for this task.
- New product discovery or scope expansion.

FINAL RESPONSE FROM THE CODING AGENT
1. Summarize what was implemented and any deliberate design/architecture decisions.
2. List every changed/added/deleted file.
3. List commands/tests run and their result.
4. Report acceptance-criteria status and any remaining real blocker/assumption.
5. Do not claim completion if required checks or critical states are missing.

- Use TanStack Query for server state, Zustand only for true global UI state, local React state for local UI, URL search params for shareable filters/sort/page/tab state, React Hook Form + Zod for forms and MSW for development network simulation.

- Preserve strict persona/context/organization isolation in query keys, caches, routes, realtime subscriptions, offline state and UI persistence.
- Never persist password, OTP, access token, refresh token, private API secret or equivalent credentials in localStorage. Never leak PII/private content into URL, telemetry or logs.
- Use existing shared primitives (SoloDataTable, SoloForm, SoloFeedback, SoloCalendar, SoloCharts, SoloUploader, SoloContentEditor, SoloPrint, SoloMap, realtime/PWA clients) instead of inventing duplicate local systems when their dependencies are already available.
- Implement Loading, Empty, Error, Not Found, Forbidden, Disabled-with-reason, Offline/Retry and plan/usage-limited states only where relevant to this task; do not add irrelevant states mechanically.
- Do not hide real blockers with fake business logic. Mocks may simulate future contracts, but the frontend must remain replaceable by real backend implementations later.

FROZEN PRODUCT RULES RELEVANT TO THIS TASK
- Task Management is full scope and acts as a shared work primitive.
- KB/Wiki supports spaces/tree, rich editor, versions, review/publish, permissions, search/tags/related, comments/mentions, owner/review reminders, templates and links to tasks/tickets/automation/onboarding.
- Forms/surveys support public forms, conditional content, consent checkbox + typed name + timestamp/snapshot, submissions/review/comments/approval.
- Custom fields, custom statuses and context tags are shared platform primitives.
- Automation supports multi-step conditions, webhooks/templates, risk levels and human approval gates; CRM supports multiple private-context pipelines, no VoIP/call log.
- Use granular roles/permissions with Owner/Manager/Academic Manager/Teacher/Finance/Support-Staff defaults plus custom roles and branch scope.
- Organization Policy Center supports inheritance/override, effective dates, sensitive policy review/publish, impact preview, versions/rollback/audit.
- Approval Center centralizes multi-step sequential/parallel approval, delegation, request-changes, low-risk bulk, SLA/escalation and self-approval prevention.
- Immutable audit is non-editable/non-deletable and captures actor/action/target/context/before-after/reason/security metadata.

TASK-SPECIFIC IMPLEMENTATION CHECKLIST
- Implement the complete frontend slice for “Automation Builder Templates Webhooks” without pulling sibling-phase scope forward unless it is required by an existing shared contract.

- Implement realistic MSW fixtures/scenarios only for the APIs this task actually consumes; do not create irrelevant endpoints just to satisfy boilerplate.

ARCHITECTURE AND INTEGRATION REQUIREMENTS
- Place code in the approved feature-first boundaries. app/ should remain routing/layout/page composition; keep feature internals inside their feature and expose only deliberate public APIs.

- Add MSW handlers/fixtures for the exact APIs used by this slice, including realistic success and meaningful failure states. Do not add unrelated mock endpoints.
- Use context-scoped TanStack Query keys and invalidation/mutation behavior. If the task is purely visual/infrastructure and consumes no server data, do not introduce artificial Query/MSW code.
- Route construction must use typed route helpers and the approved deep-link/search-param convention. Never put PII or sensitive identifiers in URLs.
- If the task touches realtime, offline, uploads, editor, maps, charts, forms, tables, print or feedback, integrate the existing shared foundation instead of implementing a parallel local version.

UI / UX REQUIREMENTS
- Use the Solo design language: modern, professional, educational, clean and readable; friendly without being childish; data-dense only where management workflows need it; no card-everywhere or decorative glassmorphism.
- Provide responsive behavior for desktop, tablet and mobile/PWA. No critical feature may be desktop-only.
- Support fa/en, true RTL/LTR, Light/Dark and reduced-motion preferences. Do not hardcode important UI copy.
- Use clear hierarchy, accessible labels/help/error copy, proper focus management, keyboard navigation and semantic HTML.

- For complex management screens, use the shared DataTable/Form/Drawer/Modal/Saved View patterns; for mobile, redesign information density rather than squeezing desktop tables unchanged.

- Verify organization/personal/subject context isolation for all data, cache keys, URLs, realtime/offline state and mutations touched by this task.
- Sanitize rich HTML, validate external URLs and protect private downloads where relevant.
- Never log/persist password, OTP, auth token, private message content, protected file contents or other sensitive data.
- Sensitive actions defined by product policy must use online-only behavior, re-authentication, confirmation/impact preview, approval and audit-aware contracts where applicable.

TESTING REQUIREMENTS
- Add focused unit tests for pure business-facing UI logic, formatters/selectors/validation introduced by this task.
- Add React Testing Library interaction tests for important component/form/permission/error behavior.
- Add or extend Playwright smoke/E2E for the critical happy path and at least the most important denial/failure path when this task creates a user workflow.
- Verify affected fa/en, RTL/LTR, Light/Dark, desktop/mobile and accessibility behavior. Use automated a11y checks plus manual keyboard/focus review for critical flows.
- If the task affects plan/capability/context/offline/realtime behavior, include fixtures/tests for those state transitions and leakage boundaries.

- No secrets or sensitive private content are introduced into client persistence, URLs, logs or telemetry.

Read docs/frontend/ENGINEERING_RULES.md and docs/frontend/PROJECT_CONTEXT.md when they exist; if this task creates them or they do not exist yet, use the frozen rules in this Markdown file and the current repository state as the source of truth. Do not rewrite previous features or shared infrastructure without a concrete need.
- Work only in /frontend unless this task explicitly updates root documentation or the /backend placeholder. Do not implement a real backend, database, server authorization, payment processor, storage service or WebSocket server.
- Use Next.js App Router + TypeScript strict + pnpm, feature-first boundaries, shared Solo design-system primitives and typed contracts.
- Use TanStack Query for server state, Zustand only for true global UI state, local React state for local UI, URL search params for shareable filters/sort/page/tab state, React Hook Form + Zod for forms and MSW for development network simulation.
- All meaningful UI text must be localized through fa/en i18n. Support true RTL/LTR, Light/Dark, Desktop/Tablet/Mobile, keyboard access and WCAG 2.2 AA.
- Use Effective Capabilities for UI access and disabled reasons. Never scatter role/plan permission logic through random components. Backend remains the future authorization source of truth.
- Preserve strict persona/context/organization isolation in query keys, caches, routes, realtime subscriptions, offline state and UI persistence.
- Never persist password, OTP, access token, refresh token, private API secret or equivalent credentials in localStorage. Never leak PII/private content into URL, telemetry or logs.
- Use existing shared primitives (SoloDataTable, SoloForm, SoloFeedback, SoloCalendar, SoloCharts, SoloUploader, SoloContentEditor, SoloPrint, SoloMap, realtime/PWA clients) instead of inventing duplicate local systems when their dependencies are already available.
- Implement Loading, Empty, Error, Not Found, Forbidden, Disabled-with-reason, Offline/Retry and plan/usage-limited states only where relevant to this task; do not add irrelevant states mechanically.
- Do not hide real blockers with fake business logic. Mocks may simulate future contracts, but the frontend must remain replaceable by real backend implementations later.

FROZEN PRODUCT RULES RELEVANT TO THIS TASK
- Keep Plan Entitlements separate from Usage Limits and calculate UI access via Effective Capabilities.
- Pricing is multi-market with Price Books (Iran/Toman and global/USD initially). Do not hardcode or invent final production prices before market research.
- Respect Teacher Free/Pro/Business and Organization Trial/Starter/Pro/Enterprise, trials, grace, downgrade no-data-loss, plan versioning, add-ons, usage/quota, optional overage off-by-default, billing center, coupons, provider abstraction, tax, refunds, invoice billing and dunning.
- Subscription billing is separate from tuition tracking and marketplace seller balance.

TASK-SPECIFIC IMPLEMENTATION CHECKLIST
- Implement the complete frontend slice for “Subscription Promotion Coupon Engine UX” without pulling sibling-phase scope forward unless it is required by an existing shared contract.
- Implement realistic MSW fixtures/scenarios only for the APIs this task actually consumes; do not create irrelevant endpoints just to satisfy boilerplate.

ARCHITECTURE AND INTEGRATION REQUIREMENTS
- Place code in the approved feature-first boundaries. app/ should remain routing/layout/page composition; keep feature internals inside their feature and expose only deliberate public APIs.
- Define or extend typed request/response/domain contracts and Zod boundaries only where this task needs them. Use standard Solo API error, money, date/time, opaque ID, concurrency and file conventions as applicable.
- Add MSW handlers/fixtures for the exact APIs used by this slice, including realistic success and meaningful failure states. Do not add unrelated mock endpoints.
- Use context-scoped TanStack Query keys and invalidation/mutation behavior. If the task is purely visual/infrastructure and consumes no server data, do not introduce artificial Query/MSW code.
- Route construction must use typed route helpers and the approved deep-link/search-param convention. Never put PII or sensitive identifiers in URLs.
- If the task touches realtime, offline, uploads, editor, maps, charts, forms, tables, print or feedback, integrate the existing shared foundation instead of implementing a parallel local version.

UI / UX REQUIREMENTS
- Use the Solo design language: modern, professional, educational, clean and readable; friendly without being childish; data-dense only where management workflows need it; no card-everywhere or decorative glassmorphism.
- Provide responsive behavior for desktop, tablet and mobile/PWA. No critical feature may be desktop-only.
- Support fa/en, true RTL/LTR, Light/Dark and reduced-motion preferences. Do not hardcode important UI copy.
- Use clear hierarchy, accessible labels/help/error copy, proper focus management, keyboard navigation and semantic HTML.
- Expose disabled/blocked reasons when useful (upgrade required, permission missing, usage limit, policy restriction, account restriction, reauth required) rather than silently hiding important affordances.
- For complex management screens, use the shared DataTable/Form/Drawer/Modal/Saved View patterns; for mobile, redesign information density rather than squeezing desktop tables unchanged.

- Verify organization/personal/subject context isolation for all data, cache keys, URLs, realtime/offline state and mutations touched by this task.
- Sanitize rich HTML, validate external URLs and protect private downloads where relevant.

- Add React Testing Library interaction tests for important component/form/permission/error behavior.
- Add or extend Playwright smoke/E2E for the critical happy path and at least the most important denial/failure path when this task creates a user workflow.
- Verify affected fa/en, RTL/LTR, Light/Dark, desktop/mobile and accessibility behavior. Use automated a11y checks plus manual keyboard/focus review for critical flows.
- If the task affects plan/capability/context/offline/realtime behavior, include fixtures/tests for those state transitions and leakage boundaries.
- Run the relevant lint, typecheck, tests and build before finishing. Do not report completion with failing required checks.

- TypeScript strict typecheck, lint and production build pass for the affected frontend.

- Relevant Loading/Empty/Error/Forbidden/Disabled/Offline/limit states are implemented and tested.
- Desktop/Tablet/Mobile, fa/en, RTL/LTR, Light/Dark and keyboard/screen-reader behavior are verified for affected UI.
- Effective Capabilities, persona/context isolation and privacy boundaries are validated for all affected actions/data.

- Real payment processor, SMS provider, map provider secret, file scanner/storage service or WebSocket server integration unless a later backend task explicitly supplies it.
